response.justification: Bogdan is clearly a talented and experienced software engineer with 20 years of technical progression, but this Principal Performance Architect role requires deep, established expertise in hardware design fundamentals entirely absent from his background. The position specifically demands SoC and IP modeling, GPU architecture analysis, and AI accelerator optimization—all specialized hardware architecture work. His career has been exclusively software-focused (web, backend, embedded tools), with no evidence of hardware design languages, system-on-chip work, or hardware-level AI workload optimization. This is a domain mismatch that cannot be resolved, even with seniority.
strengths: 20 years of technical experience with progression to staff/principal level demonstrates strong technical foundation and leadership capability
Proven ability to optimize for performance and low-latency systems (Dunnhumby experience) shows understanding of optimization trade-offs
Systems thinking and familiarity with complex infrastructure (microservices, DevOps, embedded systems) provides foundational systems knowledge
concerns: Complete absence of SoC and IP modeling experience, which is a primary responsibility of the role, and no mention of relevant hardware design languages (Verilog, VHDL, SystemVerilog)
Career entirely in software engineering with no demonstrated expertise in GPU architecture, hardware design, or AI accelerator optimization
Current AI infrastructure work at re:cinq appears to be software developer tooling (MCP frameworks) rather than hardware-level AI workload analysis or accelerator design
